Plain dates and times

Source: vignettes/articles/plain-types.Rmd
plain-types.Rmd
library(zutempo)

A plain value is a date, a time or both, with no time zone: what is written on a calendar or shown on a wall clock. zutempo has five, after Temporal’s five plain types.

R Temporal Holds Example
plain_date() PlainDate a calendar date 2026-03-07
plain_time() PlainTime a wall-clock time 09:30:00
plain_date_time() PlainDateTime both 2026-03-07T09:30:00
plain_year_month() PlainYearMonth a month of a year 2026-03
plain_month_day() PlainMonthDay a day of every year 03-07

Building them

Each type is built by the function named after it, from a string, from fields, or from another value:

plain_date("2026-03-07")
#> <zutempo_plain_date[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07
plain_date(2026, 3, 7)
#> <zutempo_plain_date[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07
plain_time(9, 30)
#> <zutempo_plain_time[1]>
#> [1] 09:30:00
plain_date_time("2026-03-07T09:30")
#> <zutempo_plain_date_time[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07T09:30:00
plain_year_month("2026-03")
#> <zutempo_plain_year_month[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03
plain_month_day("03-07")
#> <zutempo_plain_month_day[1]>
#> [1] 03-07

They are vectors, recycled as R recycles, with NA where a value is missing:

d <- plain_date(2026, 1:4, 31)
d
#> <zutempo_plain_date[4]>
#> [1] 2026-01-31 2026-02-28 2026-03-31 2026-04-30
plain_date(c("2026-03-07", NA))
#> <zutempo_plain_date[2]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07 <NA>

plain_date(2026, 1:4, 31) asked for 31 February and 31 April. By default a field out of range is constrained to its nearest valid value; overflow = "reject" makes it an error:

try(plain_date(2026, 2, 31, overflow = "reject"))
#> Error : 2026-02-31 is not a valid date (element 1)

Reading their fields

Every Temporal property is an accessor named after it:

x <- plain_date_time("2026-03-07T09:30:15.25")
year(x)
#> [1] 2026
month(x)
#> [1] 3
day_of_week(x) # 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday
#> [1] 6
day_of_year(x)
#> [1] 66
week_of_year(x)
#> [1] 10
days_in_month(x)
#> [1] 31
in_leap_year(x)
#> [1] FALSE
second(x)
#> [1] 15
millisecond(x)
#> [1] 250

Changing them

temporal_with() replaces fields and keeps the rest, constraining by default:

temporal_with(plain_date("2026-01-31"), month = 2)
#> <zutempo_plain_date[1]>
#> [1] 2026-02-28
temporal_with(x, hour = 18, minute = 0)
#> <zutempo_plain_date_time[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07T18:00:15.25
temporal_with_plain_time(plain_date_time("2026-03-07T09:30"), plain_time(12))
#> <zutempo_plain_date_time[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07T12:00:00

Arithmetic

temporal_add() and temporal_subtract() take a duration() or an ISO 8601 duration string. Months and years move through the calendar, so adding one month to 31 January gives the last day of February:

temporal_add(plain_date("2026-01-31"), "P1M")
#> <zutempo_plain_date[1]>
#> [1] 2026-02-28
temporal_add(plain_date("2026-01-31"), duration(months = 1, days = 1))
#> <zutempo_plain_date[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-01
temporal_subtract(plain_time("00:30"), "PT1H") # times wrap around midnight
#> <zutempo_plain_time[1]>
#> [1] 23:30:00

temporal_until() and temporal_since() give the duration between two values, in days by default and in larger units on request:

start <- plain_date("2026-01-31")
temporal_until(start, "2026-12-25")
#> <zutempo_duration[1]>
#> [1] P328D
temporal_until(start, "2026-12-25", largest_unit = "month")
#> <zutempo_duration[1]>
#> [1] P10M25D
temporal_until(start, "2026-12-25", largest_unit = "week")
#> <zutempo_duration[1]>
#> [1] P46W6D
temporal_since(plain_time("17:45"), "09:30")
#> <zutempo_duration[1]>
#> [1] PT8H15M

Rounding and comparing 

temporal_round(plain_time("09:47:31"), "minute", rounding_increment = 15)
#> <zutempo_plain_time[1]>
#> [1] 09:45:00
temporal_round(plain_date_time("2026-03-07T13:00"), "day")
#> <zutempo_plain_date_time[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-08T00:00:00
plain_date_compare(plain_date("2026-03-07"), "2026-03-08")
#> [1] -1
temporal_equals(plain_date("2026-03-07"), "2026-03-07")
#> [1] TRUE
sort(plain_date(c("2026-12-25", "2026-03-07", "2026-07-04")))
#> <zutempo_plain_date[3]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07 2026-07-04 2026-12-25

Year-months and month-days

A plain_year_month() is a month of a year, for things like card expiry dates; a plain_month_day() is a day that recurs every year, such as a birthday. Each becomes a date once the missing part is given:

expiry <- plain_year_month("2027-02")
days_in_month(expiry)
#> [1] 28
temporal_to_plain_date(expiry, day = 28)
#> <zutempo_plain_date[1]>
#> [1] 2027-02-28

birthday <- plain_month_day("02-29")
temporal_to_plain_date(birthday, year = 2027) # no 29 February: constrained
#> <zutempo_plain_date[1]>
#> [1] 2027-02-28
temporal_to_plain_date(birthday, year = 2028)
#> <zutempo_plain_date[1]>
#> [1] 2028-02-29

Combining them 

date <- plain_date("2026-03-07")
temporal_to_plain_date_time(date, plain_time("09:30"))
#> <zutempo_plain_date_time[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07T09:30:00
temporal_to_plain_year_month(date)
#> <zutempo_plain_year_month[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03
temporal_to_plain_month_day(date)
#> <zutempo_plain_month_day[1]>
#> [1] 03-07
temporal_to_plain_time(plain_date_time("2026-03-07T09:30"))
#> <zutempo_plain_time[1]>
#> [1] 09:30:00

A plain value has no time zone, so it does not say which moment it is. Moments and zones are in Instants and time zones.
